topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
consensus_response: The choice between GEO and LEO satellite orbits significantly impacts the performance of hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring. LEO satellites offer lower latency (<100ms) and higher channel utilization (~80%) due to their lower delay and pointing requirements, but come with increased complexity and cost. In contrast, GEO satellites have a large stationary footprint, reducing interference but increasing latency (>550ms). The introduction of Inter-Satellite Links (ISLs) in LEO constellations can reduce latency further, but also increases system complexity. Adaptive Routing Algorithms (ARA) in mesh topology LEO constellations can adapt to changing network conditions, optimizing performance and minimizing latency.
